column1: # The gate suite CI runs, with the arguments CI passes.
# Column 2: the command that runs it, the way the workflow runs it.
# Column 3: the command that runs the compiled port, once the port exists.
#           Empty means "not ported yet"; the measurement says so instead of
#           pretending the python number stands for the port.
# The flags are the ones the workflows pass, taken from .github/workflows,
# not from the documentation. A flag that only asserts a floor does not
# change the work, and a floor that the tree does not meet would make the
# gate exit 1 without changing the time; the exit code is recorded anyway.
# The gates that read an artifact the build produced (TRX files, packed
# NuGet packages, the analyzer's log) are measured against an empty
# directory of the right shape, so their number is the cost of walking the
# tree, not the cost of parsing a real artifact. They are the cheap gates,
# and the difference does not move the total.
# msbuild-evaluation-cost.py is NOT here: it measures a `dotnet build`, and
# this box has no SDK. It is listed in the README with the reason.
